For the **Mean** and **Mode** to be equal in this grouped data, the distribution should ideally be symmetric around the central class.

Identify the **Modal Class** as 25−35 (highest frequency = 10).

**Given:** Class intervals and frequencies: (15−25, 6), (25−35, 10), (35−45, x). Also, **Mean = Mode** and **x [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b15aaaca3d3ddc45f1ae78044c24777b0dcd36edc1c548ea9a302864294d2ca1.png] 

**1. Calculation of Mean:**

⇒ Midpoints (m): 20, 30, 40

⇒ Σfᵢ = 6 + 10 + x = 16 + x

⇒ Σfᵢmᵢ = (6 × 20) + (10 × 30) + (x × 40) = 120 + 300 + 40x = 420 + 40x

⇒ Mean = (420 + 40x) ÷ (16 + x)

**2. Calculation of Mode:**

⇒ Modal Class = 25−35 (as 10 is the highest frequency since x [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Empirical Relationship

For moderately skewed distributions: **Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean**.

Symmetric Distribution

In a perfectly symmetric distribution, the **Mean, Median, and Mode** are all equal.

Modal Class Property

The **Modal Class** is the interval with the highest frequency density. If frequencies are equal, the distribution is bimodal or multimodal.</p
